plan.name: Verify Python applications from relative paths
plan.summary: Use the absolute verification-project directory when relating an existing Python application's root to its driver and invocation working directory, in explicit-component invocations and both legacy binding and invocation discovery. Relative and absolute project paths must have the same preflight, prepared invocations, verification outcomes, receipts and portable fingerprints, with components declared or omitted. Preserve application containment, invocation validation, staging, original bytes and existing path semantics elsewhere; propagate path-resolution errors. Acceptance tests exercise CLI preflight and the actual Python runner with #327's Docker transport and TLC doubles, with real CLI receipts checked only when INVARIANT_PYTHON_APPLICATION_GATE_REAL=1; unavailable real checks belong to Merger work. This restores the README's existing relative-path command under D-0180, D-0181 and D-0185 without changing documented policy, so no README or SPEC edit or new policy decision is needed; any implementation decision recording belongs to the merger.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationRelativePreflightAndRun
tests.says: Explicit and omitted-component applications pass preflight from relative paths and verify.Run executes the same checks, produces the same receipt and portable fingerprint as the absolute path, and leaves application bytes unchanged.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationRelativeSession
tests.says: Preparing a session from a project loaded with a relative path succeeds and preserves the absolute path's invocations and portable provenance in explicit and legacy modes, including dot and parent-relative project paths.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationRelativeCLI
tests.says: The documented verify -out receipt relative-path command passes the same CLI preflight as its absolute form in both modes; opt-in real runs produce passing JSON and Markdown receipts with matching portable fingerprints.
